title: Informant Register distribution command
description: Body of a message on the ASB queue informantregister.requests. This is the inbound queue message contract, agreed jointly with cpp-context-results (results-event-processor), which publishes one message per resulted regular hearing. The message is a claim check: the hearing payload is fetched separately from Redis, with the results query API as fallback. Any change to this schema is a cross-team change and must be agreed with the Results team first. The narrative companion is doc/API_CONTRACTS.md; if the two disagree, this schema plus its tests win.

source.description: Publishing system. Half of the idempotency key: it namespaces requestId so a future second publisher cannot collide with Results.

requestId.description: Publisher-minted, deterministic from hearingId, hearingDay and sharedTime. A republish of the same share carries the same id; a genuine re-share produces a new sharedTime and so a new id, and must be reprocessed.

hearingId.description: The resulted hearing. With hearingDay it forms the Redis cache key and the query-API fallback path.

hearingDay.description: The hearing day this share relates to, as YYYY-MM-DD. Part of the Redis key INT_{hearingId}_{hearingDay}_result_.

sharedTime.description: ISO-8601 instant at which the hearing was shared. Becomes the register date used for subscription lookup and appears in the outbound document.

eventType.description: Hearing_Resulted only. SJP hearings are out of scope and stay in the NOWs function app. Any other value is a non-transient failure (dead-letter with reason), never a silent skip.

userId.description: OPTIONAL. The CPP user who shared the hearing results, carried so that every downstream call made for this message is attributed to that user through CJSCPPUID - which is what the function app does today: the hearing-resulted envelope's metadata userId becomes the orchestration's cjscppuid (InformantRegisterEventGridTrigger/index.js:15, InformantRegisterQueueTrigger/index.js:17) and is threaded unchanged into the payload read, the now-subscriptions read (ReferenceDataService.js:44) and the add-informant-register POST (ProcessOutboundInformantRegister/index.js:21). Optional rather than required because two legitimate producers of this message have no user to name: support replay tooling, where the replay is built by hand rather than re-sent verbatim, or is re-sent deliberately without the field because the original user has been deactivated - a replay that IS re-sent verbatim still names the user the original named, and is attributed to them; and any producer build from before this field existed - the transition window. The consumer must therefore accept a message both ways, and a message carrying no userId is processed under the service's own configured system identity. A userId that IS present must be a canonical UUID; anything else is a schema violation and dead-letters like any other, because a value that cannot be an identity must not be sent as one.
